chunks: And Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the mula'anah in which her husband accuses her, disowns her child, and performs li'an with her, then afterward her husband says, 'The child is my child,' and declares himself to have been lying.

He said: 'As for the woman, she never returns to him. As for the child, I assign him back to him if he acknowledges him, and I do not leave his child with no inheritance. The son inherits from the father, but the father does not inherit from the son. His inheritance goes to his maternal uncles. And if anyone calls him a child of zina, he is flogged with the hadd punishment.'

key_terms.الِابْنُ: the son in relation to inheritance rulings
key_terms.الْمُلَاعَنَةِ: mutual imprecation between spouses in a legal case of accusation
key_terms.لِأَخْوَالِهِ: to his maternal uncles, indicating the line of inheritance mentioned here
key_terms.مِيرَاثٌ: inheritance as determined by legal kinship
key_terms.وَلَدَ الزِّنَا: child of zina; a stigmatizing accusation prohibited here
key_terms.وَلَدُهَا: her child, whose paternity is being disputed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband retracts his denial of paternity after li'an?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning li'an when a husband later retracts his denial of paternity. It states that the wife does not return to him, while the child is affiliated back to him for purposes including inheritance in one direction, and it also forbids stigmatizing the child by calling him illegitimate.
